scope: Root code/protocol/math audit and selected official primary-source reading. No financial data, fitting, tuning, simulation, result replacement or external-model review. The two same-model companion audits retain their actual input identities and limits.

sources.title: Distributed Optimization and Statistical Learning via the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers
sources.actual_read_scope: Selected source text: sections3.1–3.3 and their scaled-update, residual and stopping equations; visual page inspection: physical22/printed19. Not a full-paper reading.
sources.source_takeaway: Scaled ADMM uses primal and dual feasibility residuals with absolute/relative tolerances. Its convex optimization premises and stopping rules do not give statistical forecasting guarantees.

sources.title: cqrReg: An R Package for Quantile and Composite Quantile Regression and Variable Selection
sources.actual_read_scope: Selected title/abstract, section2.2 and AppendixA.1.1 extracts; visually inspected physical5/printed5. Not a full-paper reading. The current landing title belongs to a later version, not this v1.
sources.source_takeaway: The paper contains a quantile-loss ADMM split, including an adaptive-lasso setting. Its displayed squared-norm tolerance formula on printed5 is not copied; the present routine follows Boyd-style norm tolerances. This is not a literal ridge/mean-loss implementation from that source.

checks.finding: P(b)=mean rho_tau(y-Xb)+lambda*||beta||^2/2; only slope coordinates beta are penalized; first X column must be exactly1.

Constraint Xb+r-y=0, rho=1/n. b solves (rho X^T X+lambda diag(0,1,...))b=rho X^T(y-r-u). r uses asymmetric soft threshold tau/(n rho), (1-tau)/(n rho). u adds the primal residual. The sign of the dual residual is immaterial to its norm.

Fenchel representation uses nu in[tau-1,tau], sum nu=0. Integer ceil/floor bounds on the 2^40 denominator grid are inward for the exact stored binary tau; the final integer zero-sum check gives an exactly represented feasible point. This does not make floating-point objectives exact real arithmetic.

checks.item: Dual objective and gap independently derived
checks.finding: Let m=Z^T nu/n and e=y-Xb. D=mean(nu*y)-||m||^2/(2 lambda). With sum nu=0, P-D=mean[rho_tau(e)-nu*e]+lambda*||beta-m/lambda||^2/2. This matches the code complementarity and stationarity signs and mean normalization; the square decomposition avoids subtractive cancellation.

Both ADMM residuals and the separate stable gap must pass. Finite solve/certificate checks can reject a fit. The gap identity uses float64 and a stated roundoff tolerance; it is not an interval-arithmetic proof or a conditional-coverage certificate.

checks.item: Why the linear system has a unique exact-arithmetic solution
checks.finding: For any nonzero v, v^T[rho X^T X+lambda diag(0,I)]v=rho||Xv||^2+lambda||v_slopes||^2>0: lambda,rho>0; if v_slopes=0 then the intercept-only vector and required ones column give ||Xv||>0. This is an algebraic observation; conditioning and floating solve error still matter.

conditional_forecast validates the entire finite vector, requires ids[-1]+H<len(x), and constructs full-sequence features/cache. The used fit/query slices remain causal in the inspected records, but suffix availability can affect whether the API accepts input. It is not a prefix-only live interface. AppendixK now states this explicitly.

After training transform, indices0:25 divide by5; pairs26:28,28:30,30:32 divide bysqrt(2); magnitude25 and gap32 retain unit multiplier. Squared Euclidean distance and lexicographic(-origin,distance) choose recent exact ties. New AppendixC prose transcribes these preexisting rules; it changes no computation.

limits: Original solver executable remains byte-identical to its original freeze; no attempt is made to retrofit the immutable historical API.
No repeated testing or simulation was used to turn finite success into population validity.
The AppendixK adapter remains unimplemented; prospective outcomes and unseen compatible dealer validation remain pending.
Primary PDFs and render cache are private .scratch files, not redistribution artifacts.
